- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to dampen momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.00) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates further decline; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment shows sudden shift from negative to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.50+), model often lags; forecast should adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it; apply 1–3% downward correction to forecast.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often fails to account for sentiment-driven volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 0.3x sentiment + 0.7x price history) for correction.
